about: Hunt packs (doc 127): a pack is a named set of Velociraptor artifacts to collect for a given situation, a set of deterministic triage rules that score the collected output into prioritised findings, and the candidate response actions each finding may warrant — every action that TOUCHES an endpoint gated behind ./securax approve. Packs map to the crisis/wargame scenarios so a hunt can be launched (or auto-prepared) straight from an incident. They run in minimal/offline mode (a self-contained collector, no server) and on a fleet server. The artifacts named are stock Velociraptor artifacts; the packs are data — edit the artifacts, rules and actions, add your own. No proprietary binary is required: triage collection uses Windows.KapeFiles.Targets (open KapeFiles) and native VQL.
severity_note: Triage scores are a FIRST pass to focus a human, never a verdict: a high score means look here first. Every response action is a human decision behind ./securax approve (single-use, time-boxed, audited). AI drafts; a human approves anything irreversible.

quick-triage.name: Quick triage (any host)
quick-triage.about: The fast, low-footprint first look at one suspect host: running processes, network connections, autostarts, recent execution. Minutes, not hours; safe to run anywhere.

triage_rules.says: a process is touching LSASS — possible credential theft; isolate and dump for analysis
encoded PowerShell — decode the command before anything else
execution from a temp/cache path — common for droppers; check the parent process
rundll32 with an unusual argument — check what DLL/export it loads
a listener on a classic implant port — treat as C2 until proven otherwise

actions.action: isolate the host from the network
actions.why: stop lateral movement and C2 while you investigate

actions.action: capture volatile memory before power state changes
actions.why: RAM holds keys, injected code and live connections that a reboot destroys

ransomware-aftermath.name: Ransomware aftermath sweep
ransomware-aftermath.about: After a ransomware hit: find the foothold and the blast radius across hosts — persistence, the encryptor's traces, deleted shadow copies, lateral-movement tooling, and the earliest sign of entry — so recovery restores clean and the same door is shut.

triage_rules.says: shadow copies were deleted — a ransomware signature; find the process and time, it anchors the timeline
backup catalog deletion — the attacker went for recovery; confirm your off-site copy is intact (ransomguard)
Cobalt Strike indicator — assume hands-on-keyboard and lateral movement; widen the hunt
PsExec-style remote execution — map which hosts it reached from this one
a Tor address in the ransom note or traffic — the C2/leak channel; preserve it for the regulator and police
credential-dumping tool — rotate every credential that touched this host

actions.action: isolate every host that shows the foothold
actions.why: contain before restore; a missed host re-infects the clean estate

actions.action: prove a clean off-site backup exists before any restore
actions.why: never restore onto a live foothold or from an encrypted copy

actions.action: force-rotate credentials seen on affected hosts
actions.why: dumped credentials are the attacker's way back

payment-fraud-persistence.name: Payment-rail fraud — foothold & persistence
payment-fraud-persistence.about: After fraudulent outward payments: hunt the hosts that touch the payment rail and the maker/checker terminals for the foothold that let it happen — persistence, remote access, injected processes, and tampering with the terminals or logs — so you can tell the regulator and police how, and shut it.

triage_rules.says: remote-access tool on a payment terminal — confirm it is sanctioned; a common fraud vector
remote-access tool on a payment terminal — confirm it is sanctioned
a keylogger indicator near a maker/checker terminal — operator credentials may be compromised
a scheduled task was created — a persistence foothold; check what it runs and when
event logs were cleared — anti-forensics; note the gap and pull the SIEM copy

actions.why: stop further fraudulent release while preserving the host for forensics

actions.action: preserve the terminal image with chain-of-custody
actions.why: the police production notice will ask for it; collect it admissibly now

lateral-movement-sweep.name: Lateral-movement & persistence sweep (fleet)
lateral-movement-sweep.about: A fleet-wide hunt for how far an intruder moved and what they left to get back in: remote-execution traces, new services and tasks, run-key and WMI persistence, and anomalous authentication — the sweep you run across every host once one is found compromised.

triage_rules.says: WMI event-consumer persistence — stealthy and fileless; remediate across every host that has it
WinRM/PowerShell remoting activity — map the source and destination of the movement
remote interactive (RDP) logon — correlate the account and source IP with your baseline
a newly installed service — a classic persistence and remote-exec foothold; verify it is sanctioned

actions.action: quarantine the persistence mechanism on every host that shows it
actions.why: leave one and the intruder returns; remediate the whole set at once

actions.action: disable and investigate the implicated accounts
actions.why: cut the credential the movement rode on

service-outage.name: Service outage — attack or accident?
service-outage.about: When a service falls over, the first question is whether it is an accident or an attack wearing the mask of one: a wiper, resource exhaustion, a killed service, a deleted config or a saturating process. This separates the two fast so you recover down the right path and do not treat a breach as a glitch.

triage_rules.says: a service was stopped by a command, not a crash — look at who and when; sabotage masquerades as an outage
a filter driver was unloaded — a tampering/EDR-blinding step; check what ran next
a format/wipe command — this is destruction, not a fault; switch to the ransomware/wiper path and preserve what remains
secure-wipe of free space — anti-forensics/destruction; image before anything is overwritten

actions.action: preserve the host image before restoring the service
actions.why: if it is destruction, restoring over it loses the evidence of how

actions.action: isolate the host if a tampering or wipe signal fired
actions.why: a masked attack spreads while you treat it as an outage

insider-misuse.name: Insider data misuse
insider-misuse.about: When a trusted account may have taken data it should not, the signals are different from an intrusion: mass reads, bulk copy to removable media or personal cloud, archiving before exfil, and access outside the person's role or hours. This gathers them for a defensible, proportionate look — people, not just machines, so handle with HR and legal.

triage_rules.says: a USB mass-storage device was attached — correlate with large file reads around that time
archive creation — staging before exfiltration; check its size and contents list
a cloud-sync/exfil tool on an endpoint that should not have it — a strong exfiltration signal
a personal-cloud client — unsanctioned data egress; confirm against policy

actions.action: preserve the endpoint and the access logs with HR and legal present
actions.why: an insider case is an HR/legal matter first; evidence handling must be defensible and proportionate

actions.action: suspend the account's data access pending review
actions.why: stop ongoing egress without tipping off before the review is set up

supply-chain-compromise.name: Supply-chain / software compromise
supply-chain-compromise.about: When a trusted vendor update or signed component may be the entry, the hunt is for the thing that should be safe behaving badly: an update process spawning a shell, a signed binary from the wrong path, a new scheduled task or service installed by an installer, or a vendor agent making unexpected network connections — across every host that runs it.

triage_rules.says: an installer ran — correlate with what it created; a trojanised update installs its foothold this way
a shell spawned by an update/installer process — updates should not spawn shells; trace the parent
a signed-looking binary running from a user-writable path — a common trojanised-component location
beaconing from a vendor/agent process — the update channel may be the C2; isolate and widen across every host that runs it

actions.action: quarantine the suspected component across every host that runs it
actions.why: a supply-chain foothold is on the whole fleet, not one host; remediate the set

actions.action: block the vendor update channel pending vendor confirmation
actions.why: if the update channel is the C2, stop it without breaking unaffected systems more than needed
